title: Spell Recipe Database
description: Each spell is a 'recipe': core (sigil or central sign) + a set of signs with count/placement/orientation + symmetry. The matcher compares the user's composition against these recipes. 'composition' uses: { core, signs:[{id,count,placement,orientation,inverted}], symmetry }. placement ∈ {around, top, bottom, sides, front, back, ring, alternating, surrounds, satellite}. confidence indicates how well the glyph is KNOWN/certain (completeness of the recipe). 'origin' is the PROVENANCE tier — WHERE the recipe data came from: 'canon' = taken directly from the manga/anime; 'wiki' = obtained from the fan wiki at witchhatatelier.telepedia.net (fan-curated from canon — this is where essentially all current catalog recipes came from); 'fan' = a purely fan-invented spell (not canon, reference only, excluded from this matcher catalog). origin is INDEPENDENT of confidence: a wiki-sourced recipe can still be high-confidence, and recipe uncertainty is recorded in 'confidence', not by downgrading origin. 'source' is a free-text citation (telepedia URL + manga debut chapter, character/arc, or who reconstructed it).

spells.name: Purify
spells.source: telepedia 'Purify' (unofficial name): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Purify — manga debut ch. 61 (per wiki). Water spell that purifies water by separating out the contaminants. Signs: Purify, Collection (docs/signs.md); Water sigil (docs/sigils.md).
spells.effect: Draws in wastewater and separates the impurities out of it; the contaminants pile up near the seal, leaving the water clean.

spells.name: Water Orb
spells.source: telepedia 'Water Orb' (unofficial name): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Water_Orb — manga debut ch. 53 (per wiki). Creates an invisible spherical container holding free-floating water.
spells.effect: Gathers water into a free-floating spherical container held above the glyph, with no physical vessel.

spells.name: Pyreball Seal
spells.source: telepedia 'Pyreball Seal': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Pyreball_Seal — manga debut ch. 8 (per wiki); cast by Coco under Qifrey's instruction to cook carapace yams. Levitating, self-fueling ball of flame.
spells.effect: Hovers a self-fueling ball of flame above the glyph and lifts light objects set over it — a floating stove.

spells.name: Snugstone Spell
spells.source: telepedia 'Snugstone Spell' (unofficial name): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Snugstone_Spell — manga debut ch. 18 (per wiki); invented by Olruggio. Radiates flameless warmth. Signs: Radial, Column (docs/signs.md).
spells.effect: Radiates gentle, flameless warmth evenly in all directions, calibrated to the seal size so it never burns.

spells.name: Flame Shot Seal
spells.source: telepedia 'Flame Shot Seal': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Flame_Shot_Seal — manga debut ch. 63 (per wiki); Coco's spell against the valance leech, a directional flame between a beam and a fireball.
spells.effect: Throws a directed column of flame forward; flanking Region signs confine the magic to the space ahead so it reaches farther.

spells.name: Spiraling Flame
spells.source: telepedia 'Spiraling Flame': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Spiraling_Flame — manga debut ch. 6 (per wiki); cast by Agott in the Illusory Labyrinth. Aimable spiraling column of flame.
spells.effect: Produces an aimable, spiraling column of flame — a mind-guided jet of fire that corkscrews as it travels (the sign of wind acts as a 'whirlwind keystone').

spells.name: Rainbringer Seal
spells.source: telepedia wiki 'Rainbringer Seal' (雨生み ameumi): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Rainbringer_Seal — manga ch. 28 p. 10; never seen cast, shown in the mural of the apprentices' arsenal while discussing how to cure Euini of the scalewolf curse (Serpentback Cave arc).
spells.effect: Generates a localized shower of rain down into the area around the seal.

spells.name: Rising Platform of Water
spells.source: telepedia wiki 'Rising Platform of Water' (水の昇り台): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Rising_Platform_of_Water — manga ch. 25 p. 16, ch. 28 p. 11; used by Richeh's old master and apprentices to traverse the floating mountains of the Dadah Range (Consent of the Crown), later shown in a spell collage during the Second Pentagram Test arc. docs/sigils.md:41, docs/signs.md:34, docs/signs.md:55.
spells.effect: Generates a rising column of water that lifts the object the seal is drawn on straight up into the air.

spells.name: Rising Wave
spells.source: telepedia 'Rising Wave' (unofficial name): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Rising_Wave — manga debut ch. 27 (per wiki); Qifrey vs. Sasaran, Serpentback Cave arc. Diagonal surge of water that launches the caster.
spells.effect: Drives a surge of water diagonally upward, launching the caster into the air.

spells.name: Water Bolt
spells.source: telepedia 'Water Bolt' (unofficial name): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Water_Bolt — manga debut ch. 24 (per wiki); Qifrey vs. the Ancients of Romonon, Serpentback Cave. Fires water arrows; drawn with the Water Pen.
spells.effect: Fires a fast, horizontal volley of water arrows straight ahead from a seal drawn flat on the ground.

spells.name: Water Horse
spells.source: telepedia 'Water Horse Spell': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Water_Horse_Spell — manga debut ch. 46 (per wiki); Qifrey's water horse carriage to the Silver Eve festival. Recipe (incl. 2 unidentified signs) from the app JSON export.
spells.effect: Forms a steerable horse of water — a Horse decorative sigil over a water core — that can pull a vehicle (e.g. the water horse carriage Qifrey used to reach the Silver Eve festival).
spells.notes: Two-sigil spell: a water core plus a Horse decorative sigil (the shape-giver, which carries the canon 'can pull loads' utility). The catalog matcher keys on the core + sign multiset, so the Horse sigil is recorded here rather than in signs[]. Signs from the app JSON export: Column ×2 (horizontal, flanking the horse at the top), Region (direction) ×2 (bottom), plus the two unidentified signs — Unknown Sign 1 ×2 (mirrored left/right pair on the sides) and Unknown Sign 2 ×3 (line-shaped, bottom row).

spells.name: Water Pen
spells.source: telepedia 'Water Pen' (unofficial name): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Water_Pen — manga debut ch. 24 (per wiki); Qifrey's tool vs. the gilded people of Romonon, Serpentback Cave. Dagger/nib-shaped glob of water. Recipe (incl. unidentified signs) from the app JSON export.
spells.effect: Conjures a hand-held, dagger / pen-nib-shaped glob of water that hovers below the seal at an angle; pour conjuring ink into it and it becomes a giant brush for drawing very large seals on any surface (Qifrey's tool in Serpentback Cave).
spells.notes: Water tool spell (unofficial name). A water core metered out at the top by a Dispersion sign flanked by two horizontal Columns, enclosed by an arc-shaped unidentified sign on each side (Unknown Sign 4, a mirrored pair) and pointed below by a triangle-like unidentified sign (Unknown Sign 3). Dispersion+Columns meter and gather the water into one coherent body; the three unidentified signs (Unknown Sign 4 ×2 + Unknown Sign 3 ×1) encode the dagger/nib shape and angled hover, so the engine flags the deduced effect as incomplete. Drawn with the ring open as a prepared, hand-held tool. Recipe from the app JSON export.

spells.name: Watershot Seal
spells.source: telepedia 'Watershot Seal' (unofficial name): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Watershot_Seal — manga debut ch. 3 (per wiki); Coco's first spell, the misfire that soaked Agott.
spells.effect: Projects a jet of water out of the seal — straight up when the Column ring is balanced, leaning toward whichever column is drawn longer (Coco's first spell; the misfire that soaked Agott).
spells.notes: Coco's first spell at Qifrey's Atelier (unofficial name). A water core ringed by eight inward Column signs. Balanced ⇒ straight-up jet; this documented build enlarges the south column (scale 2.35) so the jet leans toward it — the direction-by-size lesson (signs.md:34) that becomes the Skysoaring Seal. The lone oversized column reads as directional-bias magnitude ~0.18 toward the column, just under the engine's 0.25 'biased' threshold, so the engine reports it 'balanced' — override per canon.

spells.name: Vapor Bubble Spell
spells.source: telepedia 'Vapor Bubble Spell': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Vapor_Bubble_Spell — introduces the Cool and Gather signs (vol. 12 bonus). Two-saucer dew-still that condenses humid air into fresh water.
spells.effect: A two-circle dew-still: the outer Wind ring draws in humid air (Gather), channels it (Column) and chills it past its dew point (Cool); the nested Water core collects the condensate into a single globule of fresh water.
spells.notes: Canon (volume 12 bonus; introduces the Cool and Gather signs). A nested two-circle spell: inner closed circle = Water core (collection basin); outer open circle = Wind ×2 sigils + 2 Gather + 4 Column + 4 Cool. Harvests atmospheric moisture in water's cheap collect mode. The matcher keys on core + sign multiset, so the two outer Wind sigils (role:sigil) are recorded here in notes, not the sign list.

spells.name: Qifrey's Water Dragon
spells.source: telepedia wiki 'Qifrey's Water Dragon': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Qifrey%27s_Water_Dragon — manga ch. 7, anime ep. 5; Qifrey subdues the dragon attacking Coco in the Illusory Labyrinth. Recipe reconstructed by the wiki from partial/angled on-panel views (their stated method).
spells.effect: Draws water from nearby clouds (and likely bodies of water) and shapes it into a giant dragon, which settles into a water lily before the spell ends. Qifrey uses it to subdue the dragon attacking Coco in the Illusory Labyrinth.
spells.notes: Multi-sigil water spell. The engine core is the Dragon decorative sigil (the shape-giver); the actual substance is Water ×4 sigils ringed at N/E/S/W, plus a modified Water Flower (flower_water) decorative sigil that settles the spent water into a lily. The matcher keys on core + sign multiset, so those role:sigil sigils are recorded here, not in signs[]. Runs in water's cheap COLLECT mode: the 4 Convergence signs converge nearby cloud-water to a point so the Water sigils can incorporate it; Enlarge grows the dragon; the 8 balanced Columns dictate its direction. Dye: Azuremoon Flower (duration).

spells.name: Boulder Stretch Rope
spells.source: telepedia 'Boulder Stretch Rope': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Boulder_Stretch_Rope — manga debut ch. 21 (per wiki); Richeh's spell; shapes stone into a flexible ribbon (cross the serpentback-cave gap; capture Wolf Euini).
spells.effect: Shapes a piece of existing stone into a long, flexible ribbon — a rope of rock used to span a gap or bind a target.
spells.notes: Canon earth spell invented by Richeh. A single large Weave keystone wrapped around an Earth core transmutes rigid stone into a flexible ribbon. Runs in earth's manipulate mode (sigils.md:53) — needs a real boulder/rock to act on, it cannot conjure stone. Richeh used it to cross the gap in the serpent-back cave; Agott, Coco & Tetia used it to capture Wolf Euini. Same Weave sign as Crystal Ribbon and Light Tracer on different substances.

spells.name: Integration
spells.source: telepedia 'Integration' (unofficial name): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Integration — manga debut ch. 17 (per wiki); created by Tartah & Coco to identify powdered herbs. The inverse of the Wall Breaker Seal.
spells.effect: Temporarily reassembles a powdered/smashed substance back into the shape of the object it originally came from — used to identify an unknown powder.
spells.notes: Canon earth spell (unofficial name); the inverse of the Wall Breaker Seal — same Earth core + ring of Crush keystones, but the Crush signs are INVERTED so the effect runs backwards: instead of pulverizing matter to dust, it pulls existing particles back into their source object's form. The reassembly is TEMPORARY — once the spell lapses the powder slumps back to a pile (signs.md:73). Created by Tartah & Coco to identify unlabeled powdered medicinal herbs by their reconstructed shape, after Tartah's silverwash (total colour-blindness) prevented him telling them apart. Works on ANY solid powder, not just earth's stone/sand, because earth only manipulates/rearranges existing particles — it never conjures matter (sigils.md:53).

spells.name: Sand Cage
spells.source: telepedia 'Sand Cage': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Sand_Cage — manga debut ch. 28 (per wiki); Tetia traps the Scaled Wolf Euini. Construction reconstructed (leans on unidentified signs).
spells.effect: Builds a rigid cage of sand around a target to trap it; the rigid counterpart of the Serpent's Bed of Sand ('if sand can be made soft as a bed, it can also be made rigid as a cage').
spells.notes: Canon earth spell (unofficial name); used by Tetia to trap the Scaled Wolf Euini so the atelier could attempt the inverted Scalewolf Curse. Earth manipulates, does not create (sigils.md:53), so it needs real sand/earth present. RIGIDITY comes from the INVERTED Crush signs reintegrating loose grains into a cohesive solid (temporarily; signs.md:73) — the rigid sibling of the Serpent's Bed of Sand (soft). The canon construction (per the wiki): Earth core; a pair of Columns at east and west each pointing at one another (one normal + one inverted); inverted Crush on the N-S axis between the core and the half-circle signs; an Unknown half-circle sign (catalogued here as unknown_05) at the N and S poles; and a fusion of one Column + two Region (direction) signs at each intercardinal point (modelled here as the 3 component signs). Two unknown signs => the deduced effect is flagged incomplete. confidence=medium (leans on the unidentified unknown_05 and the column/region 'fusion' decomposition).

spells.name: Serpent's Bed of Sand
spells.source: telepedia "Serpent's Bed of Sand": https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Serpent%27s_Bed_of_Sand — manga debut ch. 7 (per wiki); mixed earth-time spell created by Qifrey's four apprentices; a fluffy, self-restoring cloud of sand.
spells.effect: Mills real stone into fine sand, billows it into a huge fluffy cloud, and continually resets the cloud so it stays soft yet firm enough to hold a dragon (regaining shape once weight is removed). The soft, self-restoring sibling of the Sand Cage.
spells.notes: Canon MIXED earth-time spell; an amalgamation invented jointly by Qifrey's four apprentices (Tetia, Richeh, Coco, Agott). Multi-circle: (1) a central BILLOW CLUSTER = a Billow sign at center (canBeCenter, signs.md:123) ringed by 4 Collection signs (gather + convert material to a cloud); (2) four small WALL BREAKER satellites (Earth core + Crush + 2 Column each) that mill real ground into fine sand and feed it inward via links; (3) an enclosing empty boundary ring; (4) an outer REPETITION SEAL (4 Repetition + 4 Convergence + 8 Column) that packs the cloud firm (Convergence, signs.md:107) and continually resets it so it returns to shape under load (Repetition, signs.md:131; retconned sign->sigil in Vol.12). Earth manipulates, does not create (sigils.md:53) => needs real stone/sand present; the Crush milling is what makes rock into the sand-like state Billow can convert. Engine validity is relation-aware: the central Billow Cluster is promoted (Billow-as-center = substance), the empty mid ring is a boundary ring, and the outer repetition seal is a modifier ring => reads VALID. SOFT sibling of the Sand Cage (which uses INVERTED Crush for rigidity instead). confidence=high (well documented in manga/wiki).

spells.name: Wall Breaker Seal
spells.source: telepedia 'Wall Breaker Seal': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Wall_Breaker_Seal — manga debut ch. 6 (per wiki); Agott breaks a wall escaping the Illusory Labyrinth dragon; later Coco frees Custas from a boulder.
spells.effect: Drawn on a solid object, breaks through it and reduces the material to dust. Earth's destruction seal; the non-inverted-Crush counterpart of Integration and the destructive foil of Wall Bend.
spells.notes: Canon earth spell. Earth sigil + two Column keystones flanking it + two Crush keystones at 90 deg. NON-INVERTED Crush = pulverize to dust (Wall Breaker; signs.md:73) - inverting the Crush flips the spell to Integration (reassemble). The Columns drive the crushing force THROUGH the material so the break has reach/penetration (crush-needs-force; signs.md:34); without them Crush only crumbles on contact. Earth manipulates, does not create (sigils.md:53): the seal is drawn ON the solid it destroys. First used by Agott to break a wall escaping the Illusory Labyrinth dragon; later by Coco to free Custas from a boulder; helped inspire the Serpent's Bed of Sand (whose satellites mill rock the same way). Engine aim 'above the seal' is an artifact - the Columns drive into the wall, not upward. confidence=high (well documented in manga/wiki).

spells.name: Flying Puppet of Diversion
spells.source: telepedia 'Flying Puppet of Diversion': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Flying_Puppet_of_Diversion — manga debut ch. 6 (per wiki); Tetia diverts a dragon by casting it on her cloak and hat.
spells.effect: Makes the object the seal is drawn on dart and fly erratically through the sky (mind-piloted), with enough force to carry objects aloft. Tetia cast it on her cloak and hat as a flying decoy to divert a dragon.
spells.notes: Canon wind spell. A single large Puppet (dancing_puppet) keystone surrounding the wind sigil (surrounds=true; the one sign IS the whole form, so the engine's single-sign 'asymmetric' is an artifact). Puppet is the rare mind-control sign: it lets the drawer/last-toucher pilot the object the seal is drawn on, and its behaviour is sigil-keyed - with WIND it means aerial movement (signs.md:295). Engine grammar synergy dancing-puppet-air fires: 'With a wind element, Dancing Puppet sends objects darting through the open air.' Wind manipulates/moves air but does not create it (sigils.md:65), so it pilots the drawn object rather than conjuring wind. Sign SIZE sets power/lift (drawn large here -> can carry a cloak+hat up; engine power ~3.85 'amplified'). Same wind+puppet template as the Cloak Spell (signs.md:297) - the Cloak is worn and piloted, this is cast off as a decoy. Not forbidden (acts on an object, not a body). confidence=high (well documented in manga/wiki).

spells.name: Rainflinger
spells.source: telepedia 'Rainflinger' (水飛ばし mizutobashi): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Rainflinger — manga debut ch. 8 (old versions), retconned ch. 28 (new/current version). This recipe is the current version; the repel-vs-dry mechanism is unconfirmed and it leans on the canon-uncertain Crosshair sign.
spells.effect: Creates a water-repellent bubble around the seal, keeping its radius dry — by repelling and/or drying off the water (mechanism unconfirmed). Qifrey used it for a picnic in the rain and to dry off Brushbuddy.
spells.notes: Mixed water/fire spell, NEW/current version (ch. 28). Engine core is the Water sigil; two Fire sigils (role:sigil) sit above and below it, and a Crosshair sign flanks each side. The matcher keys on core + sign multiset, so the two Fire sigils are recorded here in notes, not in signs[]. The Crosshair confines the magic to an area of effect — the dry 'bubble' (signs.md:239) — while the Fire substance likely drives the drying/repelling of the water; canon doesn't confirm whether the water is repelled or evaporated. Two earlier, retconned versions (manga ch. 8) used an AIR-sigil-variant core with modified Fire sigils on the sides instead: a Repelling variant and a Drying variant (the latter with INVERTED fire sigils + a disconnected triangle line) — those are described in docs/spells/Rainflinger.md but not modelled here (their 'modified/variant' sigils don't map to clean ids). confidence=medium (Crosshair is canon-uncertain; repel-vs-dry mechanism unconfirmed).

spells.name: Grasping Wind
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Grasping_Wind — manga debut ch. 14; first used by Coco. Wind sigil ringed by inward-facing Pull signs.
spells.effect: Pulls a strong wind current in toward the glyph, dragging lighter objects with it; slanting the Pull signs twists the inflow into a vortex.
spells.notes: Wind spell. Wind core ringed by 4 inward Pull signs (cardinals; the wiki shows four) => the air current converges on the seal (engine: 'wind contained within the ring'). Pull stays NON-inverted: inverting Pull flips it to 'push away' (repel), the opposite effect. Pull's traced art was vertically flipped (tip at bottom); the svgPath has been corrected so a non-inverted, inward-facing Pull renders pointing toward the center. Slanting the Pull signs adds spin -> a pulling vortex (canon). Count sets ring evenness, not power (engine power = average sign SIZE). confidence=high.

spells.name: Skysoaring Seal
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Skysoaring_Seal — manga debut ch. 4; Coco's Consent of the Crown test (to reach a Diadem Herb), drawn large on a sail to fly.
spells.effect: Produces directional thrust in the direction its Levitation keystone points; drawn large on something like a sail, it lifts and flies the object.
spells.notes: Wind spell. A Wind sigil sits low in the glyph with a single large Levitation sign spanning above it toward the opposite side; thrust fires in the keystone's direction (engine: 'lifted and made to levitate, above the seal'). SIZE sets lift — drawn big enough it carries large objects (a sail) into flight. The asymmetric single-keystone layout is intended (directional). confidence=high.

spells.name: Light Beam
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Light_Beam — used by Agott during magic drawing practice. Light sigil ringed by Column keystones.
spells.effect: Projects a steady column/beam of light straight up from the seal; the more precisely the glyph is drawn, the steadier the beam.
spells.notes: Light spell. Light core + a ring of 4 inward Column signs (the wiki shows four) => a vertical beam (engine: 'projected as a tight column or beam, above the seal'). The light analogue of the Watershot Seal. Adding more Columns does not change the effect or power (power = average sign size); it only makes the ring denser/even and changes the matcher count. Beam steadiness scales with drawing precision (canon). confidence=high.

spells.name: Crystal Shard
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Crystal_Shard — manga debut ch. 18; Richeh cast it during an emotional outburst after Qifrey suggested she study other magic.
spells.effect: Erupts several large, shard-like crystals suddenly out of the glyph.
spells.notes: Crystal spell. Crystal core + a ring of 4 INVERTED Column signs (the wiki shows four) => the columns drive inward and the crystal erupts as shards (engine: 'driven inward and erupts rather than projecting out'). Count affects ring evenness/coverage, not the effect or power (power = average sign size). Same inverted-column eruption template as Wind Wall. confidence=high.

spells.name: Floating Drops
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Floating_Drops — mixed water/air; manga debut ch. 16.
spells.effect: Generates water droplets that hover in the air, forming along the seal's outer ring; counteracting Region pairs pin the drops to the ring rather than letting them fall or fly off.

signs.placement: east-west, pointing inward toward the Water sigils
outer ring (paired with the inverted set, facing each other)
outer ring (paired with the normal set, facing each other)

spells.notes: Mixed water/air spell. Engine core is the Air (Wind) sigil; two Water sigils (role:sigil) flank it on the east-west axis, each fed by a Column pointing inward at it. Around the outer ring sit EIGHT opposed Region (direction) pairs -- each pair one normal + one inverted, pointing at one another -- so the net direction cancels and the conjured droplets are pinned ALONG the ring (engine: 'emerging only along the ring', bilateral). The two Water sigils are recorded here in notes (matcher keys on core + sign multiset). confidence=high.

spells.name: Bird of Light Beacon
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Bird_of_Light_Beacon — manga debut ch. 11; Agott used it at the river rescue to distract an outsider and call for help.
spells.effect: Forms a bird made of light that flies around for a while — to entertain, signal/call for help, or distract.
spells.notes: Light spell. Engine core is the Light sigil; the BIRD is the decorative shape SIGIL (bird_a, role:sigil) that gives the light the form of a bird, plus a single Dispersion sign that releases/spreads the light (engine: 'light leaks out and spreads on every side'). The matcher keys on core + sign multiset, so the bird_a sigil is recorded here in notes, not in signs[]. (Earlier draft wrongly used a 'bird' SIGN x3 -- corrected: it is one bird_a sigil + one dispersion sign.) Same 'decorative shape-sign gives the substance a body' pattern as Water Horse / Qifrey's Water Dragon. confidence=medium.

spells.name: Floatglow Lamp Seal
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Floatglow_Lamp_Seal — manga debut ch. 2 (lamp), seal shown ch. 28 (wall-anchored). This recipe is the free-floating version.
spells.effect: Creates a floating ball/beam of light held free of gravity — a flameless lamp. (Free-floating version; a wall-anchored variant also exists.)
spells.notes: Light spell, FREE-FLOATING version. Light core surrounded by alternating Float and Column signs => a beam of light that also floats free of gravity (engine: 'projected as a tight column or beam... it floats free of gravity'). A second WALL-ANCHORED version exists (seal shown ch. 28) and is not modelled here. confidence=medium (two versions; built the free-floating one).

spells.name: Sylph Shoes Seal
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Sylph_Shoes_Seal — manga debut ch. 1; drawn on Sylph Shoes (a contraption). The seal is bisected, one half per sole, and completes when the shoes touch.
spells.effect: Lets the wearer float above the ground and fly. Drawn on a pair of shoes as a bisected seal — one half on each sole — that completes and activates when the two shoes are touched together.
spells.notes: Wind spell on a CONTRAPTION (Sylph Shoes). Core = Wind Underfoot sigil (a wind variant); around it, 8 Convergence + 8 Levitation signs alternating (the wiki shows eight of each) => lift focused to a point under the wearer (engine: 'lifted and made to levitate... focused down to a single point'). Convergence's neutral orientation already points inward (defaultFacing 'outward' = tip toward center). The seal is bisected across the two soles and completes when they touch. Count sets ring density, not power. confidence=medium (contraption; bisected activation not modelled by the single-seal engine).

spells.name: Gathering Shadows
spells.source: https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Gathering_Shadows — manga debut ch. 21; seen as a component of the Mirror Cloak of Borrowshade spell.
spells.effect: Makes the object it is drawn on absorb all light that hits it, so the user can conceal themselves in shadow by covering up with the object.
spells.notes: Vision spell. Vision sigil core with Eye signs on 4 of its 8 points and Bend signs off the other 4 => the object absorbs incoming light and bends light/shadow around it for concealment (engine: 'absorbs light into shadow and bends light and shadow around its target'). Appears as a building block of the Mirror Cloak of Borrowshade. confidence=medium (concealment vision magic; ties into forbidden-adjacent borrowshade).

spells.name: Sand Bridge
spells.source: telepedia 'Sand Bridge': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Sand_Bridge — manga debut ch. 12, anime ep. 8. Niche spell; the central sigil and several signs are unidentified (catalogued here as sand_bridge sigil + unknown_06/09/10).
spells.effect: Constructs a temporary bridge out of sand, building it one pillar/section at a time to span a gap.
spells.notes: Niche earth/sand spell (manga ch. 12 / anime ep. 8). TWO-CIRCLE nested seal: an inner circle = the sand_bridge core (unidentified central sigil; element treated as earth) flanked by a Region-like unknown_06 pair; an outer coreless MODIFIER ring that shapes it. Outer ring: two large N/S Columns (raise the sand into pillars along the span axis) + 4 smaller intercardinal Columns; 4 Strengthen (reinforce to bear weight); 2 INVERTED Radial at E/W (the only known inverted Radial -- likely un-tempers/firms the structure, a DEDUCTION not canon: see the Radial lexicon Findings); 2 unknown_11 'bridge' glyphs at E/W (likely the arch/deck shape-giver); plus unidentified unknown_05 (half-circle arcs), unknown_09 (dumbbells) and unknown_10 (parallel-line marks). Earth manipulates, does not create (sigils.md:53) => needs real sand present; the build is TEMPORARY, raised one pillar at a time. Six unidentified glyph types (sand_bridge sigil + unknown_05/06/09/10/11) => engine flags the deduction incomplete. confidence=low.

spells.name: Wind Wall
spells.source: telepedia 'Wind Wall': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Wind_Wall (effect confirmed via Fandom mirror https://witch-hat-atelier.fandom.com/wiki/Wind_Wall) -- wind spell invented by Alaira; debut: Tetia briefly holds the transformed Euini. Recipe is a user reconstruction from the partial manga seal + the wiki construction description.
spells.effect: Packs and shapes the surrounding air into a standing circular wall -- a dense pressure barrier that deflects objects and contains people or animals.
spells.notes: Wind-type barrier spell invented by Alaira (debut: Tetia holds the transformed Euini). Wind core (air: moves but does NOT create air -- sigils.md:65; ambient air is the medium). Three roles: WEAVE x1 (large, surrounds core) weaves the moving air into one continuous ribbon = the wall surface; CONVERGENCE x6 (back half, upright) concentrates+FIRMS the air into a dense pressurized sheet (canon ties Convergence to wall-of-wind: 'manifest about or from a single point' + 'pack loose particles tightly/rigid' -- signs.md:107); COLUMN x6 (front half, INVERTED) erupts air outward on all sides (inverted column ~= dispersion, signs.md:34) so it encloses as a ring rather than firing a jet. Result is a PRESSURE barrier, not a solid object: deflects/contains but penetrable with force and temporary. Engine 'aim down/beam skews down' is an ARTIFACT (inverted columns spread, don't beam). RECONSTRUCTION not a decoded seal: Wind core + inverted Columns front + Convergence back are from the wiki text/partial panel; counts (6+6) are guesses; the enclosing sign's identity is the main open question -- WEAVE is the best functional fit ('surrounds the central sigil') but the wiki calls it 'a semicircular sign with small details on its edges,' which RADIAL (nested arcs) matches more literally. confidence=medium.

spells.name: Warmth-Retention Seal
spells.source: telepedia 'Warmth-Retention Seal': https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Warmth-Retention_Seal -- recipe is the canonical example named in the Stop sigil description (sigils.md:107).
spells.effect: Locks an object's temperature by halting only the heat aspect of its timeline -- a magical thermos: hot stays hot, cold stays cold, indefinitely, producing no flame.
spells.notes: Time-type STATE-LOCK pairing two sigils: STOP core (element time; 'outright halts time for the objects it affects' -- sigils.md:107; immaterial, acts on time/state not matter) + a FIRE sigil partner that SCOPES the halt to fire's domain (heat). Stop alone = total stasis (Time Stop / Petrification); the Fire sigil narrows it to the thermal aspect, so the target's temperature freezes without continuing to burn -- this is the exact example the source names: 'stop time for specific aspects of an object, such as changes in heat if paired with a fire sigil.' Deliberately SIGN-FREE: it suppresses a change rather than projecting/aiming a substance, so the engine's 'no signs -> raw discharge' warning is a FALSE POSITIVE here. CATALOG CAVEAT: the matcher only records a 'Match' when signCount>0 (analyze.js:117), so this sign-free spell will NOT self-match -- entry is for provenance/record. Schema has no extra-sigil field; the essential Fire partner is captured here in notes, not in composition. Works both directions (keeps cold cold as readily as hot hot). Opposite mechanism to Snugstone (which GENERATES warmth; this RETAINS it).

spells.name: Beast Warding
spells.source: telepedia 'Beast Repellent' (also called Beast Warding): https://witchhatatelier.telepedia.net/wiki/Beast_Repellent -- a common utility seal that keeps wild animals away. Listed among Mixed Spells (spells.md) and Light spells (sigils.md:31).
spells.effect: A stationary, self-lit, all-around ward: conjured light spread evenly on every side around an unidentified beast-repelling core, forming a glowing zone that wild animals avoid. Not a beam or projectile.
spells.notes: Mixed/light utility ward. Core is the UNIDENTIFIED Warding Pillar sigil (element 'unknown') -- the actual beast-repel agent; mechanism cannot be derived (CORE.md S6), so confidence=low and the effect is recorded as a reading, not fact (see docs/spells/Beast_Warding.md for ranked hypotheses). Schema has no extra-sigil field: the seal also carries TWO LIGHT sigils flanking E/W (light is create-capable/self-sufficient, 'shines outward' -- substances.md:64-66), which make it self-lit; they are captured here in notes, not in composition. The 4 COLUMN signs are INVERTED -> magic 'driven inward and erupts... emitting on all sides' ~= Dispersion (signs-directional.md:18-22), so the light spreads omnidirectionally rather than firing. The two UNKNOWN_12 ward-crosses sit at the N/S poles. ENGINE ARTIFACT: facts report aim 'above the seal'; override -- 4 balanced inverted Columns confine/spread, they do not beam (signs-directional.md:36-37), and lateral aim on light is also an artifact (substances.md:73). Net aim: omnidirectional. Mechanically the INVERSE of Light Beam (same light, spread as a ward field instead of focused into a beam); sits in the 'light as steady emission' family with Floatglow Lamp and Bird of Light Beacon.
